items.title: Section: Contemplation of Impurity Closes; Loving-Kindness Contemplation Opens

items.zh: 是名勤修不淨觀者，尋思六事差別所緣毘鉢舍那。云何勤修慈愍觀者，尋思六事差別所緣毘鉢舍那？謂依慈愍增上正法聽聞受持增上力故，由欲利益安樂意樂，於諸有情作意與樂，發起勝解，是慈愍相。
items.en: This is called the insight, with objects differentiated by the six things, of one who diligently cultivates the contemplation of impurity. How does one who diligently cultivates loving-kindness contemplation investigate insight with objects differentiated by the six things? That is, by the empowering force of having heard and upheld the excellent teaching on loving-kindness, out of a heartfelt wish for beings' benefit and happiness, one directs the mind towards giving all beings happiness, giving rise to a vivid understanding — this is the mark of loving-kindness.

items.zh: 若能如是解了其義，如是名為於諸慈愍尋思其義。
彼既如是解了義已，復能思擇：此為親品、此為怨品、此中庸品。是一切品，皆他相續之所攝故，於中發起外事勝解。又若親品，名為內事；怨、中庸品，名為外事。如是名為於諸慈愍尋思其事。
items.en: Having thus understood its meaning, one is further able to discern: this is the category of loved ones, this the category of enemies, this the neutral category. All these categories belong to the mental continuum of others, so with respect to them one gives rise to a vivid understanding of them as an external matter. Further, the category of loved ones is called an inner matter; the categories of enemies and neutral persons are called an external matter.

items.title: The Particular Characteristic of Loving-Kindness: Wishing Happiness Across Three Levels

items.zh: 復能思擇：如是三品，若無苦樂欲求樂者，願彼得樂。今於此中，有饒益相，名為親品；不饒益相，名為怨品；俱相違相，名中庸品。如是三品，若無苦樂欲求樂者，略有三種欲求樂心差別可得。一者、欲求欲界諸樂；二者、欲求色界有喜勇悅諸樂；三者、欲求離喜諸樂。如是若於欲樂匱乏，願彼皆得無罪欲樂。若於有喜、離喜諸樂有所匱乏，當知亦爾。是名尋思慈愍自相。
items.en: One further discerns: as for these three categories, if any are without pain or pleasure yet desire pleasure, one wishes that they attain it. Herein, what has a beneficial mark is called the category of loved ones; what has a harmful mark is called the category of enemies; what has neither mark is called the neutral category. As for these three categories, if without pain or pleasure yet desiring pleasure, there are, in brief, three kinds of desire for pleasure to be found: first, desiring the pleasures of the desire realm; second, desiring the joyous, exultant pleasures of the form realm; third, desiring the pleasures free of joy. Thus, if lacking desire-realm pleasure, one wishes they attain blameless desire-realm pleasure; and likewise for lacking the pleasures with joy or free of joy. This is called investigating the particular characteristic of loving-kindness.

items.title: Section: The Universal Characteristic — Why an Enemy Can Be Wished Happiness at All

items.zh: 復審思擇：若諸親品、若諸怨品、若中庸品，我於其中皆當發起相似性心、平等性心。何以故？我若作意與親品樂，此未為難；於中庸品作意與樂，亦未甚難；若於怨品作意與樂，乃甚為難。我於怨品尚應作意願與其樂，何況親品及中庸品而不與樂。何以故？此中都無能罵、所罵、能瞋、所瞋、能弄、所弄、能打、所打，唯有音聲、唯有名字。
items.en: One further carefully discerns: whether they be loved ones, enemies, or neutral persons, I should give rise, towards all of them equally, to a mind of resemblance and a mind of equanimity. Why? Because if I direct my mind to give happiness to a loved one, this is not difficult; to a neutral person, this is also not very difficult; but to give happiness to an enemy is truly difficult. Yet if I should even direct my mind to wish happiness upon an enemy, how much more so for a loved one or neutral person! Why? Because in truth there is here no one who reviles and no one reviled, no one who is angry and no one who is the object of anger, no one who mocks and no one mocked, no one who strikes and no one struck — there is only sound, only names.

items.title: Equanimity Mind: Shared Impermanence, Shared Suffering, and No Fixed Enemies

items.zh: 又我此身，隨所生起，有色麁重四大所造，隨所住處，便為如是觸所逼惱。略有二觸，謂音聲觸，及手足塊刀杖等觸。是身及觸皆是無常，能為如是不饒益者亦是無常。又復一切有情之類，皆有生老病死等法，本性是苦；故我不應於本性苦諸有情上，更加其苦，而不與樂。
items.en: Further, this body of mine, however it arises, is made of coarse, heavy great elements, and wherever it dwells, it is thereby afflicted by such contacts as these … Both this body and its contacts are impermanent, and whoever brings about such harm is likewise impermanent. Further, every kind of being has birth, old age, sickness, and death, and is, by nature, suffering. I should not, then, add further suffering upon beings whose very nature is already suffering, and withhold happiness from them.

items.zh: 又亦不應不與怨家作善知識、不攝一切有情之類以為自體。又世尊言：我不觀見如是種類有情可得。無始世來經歷生死，長時流轉，不互相為或父、或母、兄弟、姊妹，若軌範師，若親教師、若餘尊重、似尊重者。由是因緣，一切怨品無不皆是我之親品。又怨、親品，無有決定真實可得。何以故？親品餘時轉成怨品；怨品餘時轉成親品，是故一切無有決定。
items.en: Further, the World-Honoured One said: "I see no being of any kind who has not, across beginningless time and long ages of transmigration through birth and death, at some point been my father, my mother, my brother, or my sister" … For this reason, there is not a single one among all the categories of enemies who is not also my loved one. Further, the categories of enemy and loved one have no fixed, real existence to be found. Why? Because a loved one may at another time turn into an enemy, and an enemy may at another time turn into a loved one — hence none of it is fixed at all.

items.zh: 故我今者，應於一切有情之類，皆當發起平等性心、平等性見；及起相似利益意樂、安樂意樂與樂勝解。是名尋思慈愍共相。

items.title: Section: Category, Time, and Principle — Loving-Kindness Contemplation Closes, and With It, Fascicle 30

items.zh: 復審思擇：我若於彼不饒益者發生瞋恚，便為顛倒，黑品所攝，是有諍法，廣說如前。我若於彼不起瞋恚，便無顛倒，白品所攝，是無諍法，廣說如前。如是名為尋思慈愍黑品、白品。復審思擇：諸過去世求欲得樂有情之類，彼皆過去，我當云何能與其樂？諸現在世有情之類，我今願彼盡未來世，於一切時常受快樂。
items.en: One further carefully discerns: if I give rise to anger towards one who has harmed me, this is a distortion, belonging to the dark category … If I do not give rise to anger towards them, this is free of distortion, belonging to the bright category … One further carefully discerns: beings of the past who sought and wished for happiness are already gone — how, then, could I give them happiness? As for beings of the present, I now wish that, throughout every future time, they constantly receive happiness.

items.zh: 復審思擇：此中都無我及有情，或求樂者、或與樂者；唯有諸蘊、唯有諸行，於中假想施設言論，此求樂者、此與樂者。又彼諸行，業煩惱等以為因緣。如是名依觀待道理尋思慈愍。若於慈愍善修、善習、善多修習，能斷瞋恚。如是名依作用道理尋思慈愍。如是之義，有至教量；我內智見現轉可得；比度量法，亦有可得。如是名依證成道理尋思慈愍。又即此法成立法性、難思法性、安住法性。謂修慈愍能斷瞋恚，不應思議、不應分別；應生勝解。如是名依法爾道理尋思慈愍。是名勤修慈愍觀者，尋思六事差別所緣毘鉢舍那。
items.en: One further carefully discerns: herein there is truly no self and no being — no one who seeks happiness, no one who gives it; there are only aggregates, only conditioned formations, within which words are provisionally set up: "this one seeks happiness," "this one gives happiness." Further, these formations arise through karma, affliction, and the like as causes and conditions … If one cultivates loving-kindness well, practises it well, and repeatedly practises it well, one is able to sever hatred … And this very teaching establishes its own nature, a nature difficult to conceive, a nature on which the establishing of things rests: that cultivating loving-kindness can sever hatred should not be debated or analysed away, but should give rise to confident understanding. This is called the insight, with objects differentiated by the six things, of one who diligently cultivates loving-kindness contemplation.

blocks.text: The same six-fold investigation applied to loving-kindness. Fascicle 30 ends today.
"Out of a heartfelt wish for beings' benefit and happiness, one directs the mind towards giving all beings happiness." The substance: three categories of person, loved ones, enemies, and neutral.

For those without pain or pleasure who desire pleasure, one wishes them happiness, at three levels: "the pleasures of the desire realm; the joyous pleasures of the form realm (the first two absorptions); the pleasure free of joy (the third)".

subs.head: Shared characteristic: why an enemy too

blocks.text: "Whether loved ones, enemies, or neutral persons, I should give rise towards all equally to a mind of resemblance." When someone reviles me, "in truth there is here no one who reviles and no one reviled; there is only sound, only names". Master Cháng Bǎi explains.

"This body of mine is made of coarse, heavy elements, afflicted by contact"; so is everyone's. "Every being has birth, old age, sickness, and death, and is by nature suffering." The Buddha said: "I see no being who has not, across beginningless time, at some point been your mother, father, brother, sister, teacher." And "a loved one may at another time turn into an enemy, and an enemy into a loved one": there are no fixed enemies.

"If I give rise to anger towards one who has harmed me, this is distortion, belonging to the dark category." And finally: "Herein there is truly no self and no being: no one who seeks happiness, no one who gives it; there are only aggregates, only conditioned formations."

This fascicle is the heart of the Śrāvaka Stage's meditation teaching: how a teacher receives a student, the nine stages of calm, the four kinds of insight, and the six-fold investigation applied to impurity and loving-kindness. Fascicle 31 continues with the other objects.

quiz.q: Loving-kindness arises "from a wish for benefit and happiness." How do the masters distinguish the two?
options: Miào Jìng: benefit is present, happiness future; Cháng Bǎi agrees and adds benefit may be a change of mind, happiness of life
quiz.why: "Out of a heartfelt wish for beings' benefit and happiness, one directs the mind towards giving all beings happiness — this is the mark of loving-kindness." Venerable Miào Jìng: benefit refers to the present, happiness to the future. Master Cháng Bǎi agrees and adds: or benefit is a change in thinking, happiness a change in living.

quiz.q: What are the three desires for pleasure, and why are the fourth absorption and above not mentioned?
options: desire-realm pleasures, joyous form-realm pleasures, joy-free pleasures; beyond the fourth absorption there is no pleasure
quiz.why: "First, desiring the pleasures of the desire realm; second, desiring the joyous, exultant pleasures of the form realm; third, desiring the pleasures free of joy." Venerable Miào Jìng: three kinds of pleasure; the fourth absorption and above are not mentioned because there is no pleasure there.

quiz.q: "Only sound, only names" — what image does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: words are like an echo in an empty valley — only sound, only names
quiz.why: "In truth there is here no one who reviles and no one reviled … there is only sound, only names." Master Cháng Bǎi: words are like an echo in an empty valley — only sound, only some names.

quiz.q: Equanimity mind says all beings are "by nature suffering." Which suffering do the masters say this is?
options: both: the suffering of conditioned existence — impermanent aggregates breeding all affliction
quiz.why: "Further, every kind of being has birth, old age, sickness, and death, and is, by nature, suffering." Venerable Miào Jìng: this coarse suffering includes conditioned, changing, and painful suffering — but here only conditioned suffering is meant. Master Cháng Bǎi: this is conditioned suffering — because of these changing, impermanent aggregates, all affliction can arise.

quiz.q: Enemy and loved one "are not fixed." What saying does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: a near neighbour beats a far relative
in politics there are no permanent enemies, nor permanent friends
quiz.why: "A loved one may at another time turn into an enemy, and an enemy may at another time turn into a loved one — hence none of it is fixed at all." Master Cháng Bǎi: as people say, in politics there are no permanent enemies and no permanent friends.

quiz.q: "安住法性" is rendered "a nature in which one abides." How do the lectures read it?
options: Miào Jìng: buddhas set up words expressing the nature so we can study and attain the path; Cháng Bǎi: it is a bridge leading beings to nirvāṇa's truth
quiz.why: "This very teaching establishes its own nature, a nature difficult to conceive, a nature in which one abides." Venerable Miào Jìng: the great wisdom of buddhas and bodhisattvas set up words to express this nature, so we can study, practice, and attain the path — that is 安住法性. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is a bridge enabling beings to reach the truth of nirvāṇa. The lectures stress "establishing and transmitting," unlike the English "abiding in."
